    Solvers

    Mesh containers for finite-element solvers.

    FEMBase plots and queries a Tatva mesh. HeightMapFEMBase builds that mesh from a scan. MeshFEMBase loads a surface mesh and can tetrahedralize it.

    FEMBase #

    Bases: ABC

    Base class for solvers that operate on one or more Tatva meshes.

    This class deliberately knows nothing about where the mesh came from or which physics is solved on it.

    class FEMBase(ABC):
    """Base class for solvers that operate on one or more Tatva meshes.

    This class deliberately knows nothing about where the mesh came from or
    which physics is solved on it.
    """

    CELL_TYPE: CellType

    def __init__(self):
        """Create a solver with no mesh stored yet."""
        self.meshes: Mesh | list[Mesh] | None = None

    def boundary_geometry(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Return the exterior boundary of one mesh of this solver's cell type.

        Args:
            mesh: Tatva mesh to query. It is not read from ``self.meshes``.

        Returns:
            Boundary connectivity and unit outward normals.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``CELL_TYPE`` has no boundary definition, or if a
                boundary face has a zero normal.

        """
        return boundary_geometry(mesh, self.CELL_TYPE)

    def plot(
        self,
        *,
        backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        values=None,
        data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
        surface_elements=None,
        label: str = "values",
        dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
        plane: Plane = "xy",
        cmap: str = "managua",
        show_edges: bool = False,
        lighting: bool | None = None,
        title: str | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "mesh.pdf",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
    ):
        """Plot one mesh, with no knowledge of where it came from.

        ``mesh=None`` uses ``self.meshes``. ``index`` selects an entry when that
        value is a list. ``values`` are colored on the nodes or the cells according
        to ``data_location``.

        Args:
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
            index: Entry to draw when ``mesh`` is a list. Default: the first entry.
            values: Scalar field to color. The mesh is drawn uncolored when omitted.
            data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. Required when ``values`` is
                set and the plotter cannot infer it.
            surface_elements: Optional face connectivity used instead of the mesh
                cells. Each row is one face.
            label: Color-bar label. Default: ``"values"``.
            dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
            plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
                ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
            cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
            title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name, including the extension. Default: ``"mesh.pdf"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty.
            TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

        """
        if mesh is None:
            mesh = self.meshes
            if mesh is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
                )

        idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

        if isinstance(mesh, list):
            mesh = mesh[idx]
        elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

        return plot_tatva_mesh(
            mesh,
            cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
            backend=backend,
            values=values,
            data_location=data_location,
            surface_elements=surface_elements,
            label=label,
            title=title,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            dimensionality=dimensionality,
            plane=plane,
            cmap=cmap,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            lighting=lighting,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    def plot(
    self,
    *,
    backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
    ax=None,
    plotter=None,
    mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
    index: int | None = None,
    values=None,
    data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
    surface_elements=None,
    label: str = "values",
    dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
    plane: Plane = "xy",
    cmap: str = "managua",
    show_edges: bool = False,
    lighting: bool | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "mesh.pdf",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Plot one mesh, with no knowledge of where it came from.

    ``mesh=None`` uses ``self.meshes``. ``index`` selects an entry when that
    value is a list. ``values`` are colored on the nodes or the cells according
    to ``data_location``.

    Args:
        backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
        ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
        plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
        mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
        index: Entry to draw when ``mesh`` is a list. Default: the first entry.
        values: Scalar field to color. The mesh is drawn uncolored when omitted.
        data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. Required when ``values`` is
            set and the plotter cannot infer it.
        surface_elements: Optional face connectivity used instead of the mesh
            cells. Each row is one face.
        label: Color-bar label. Default: ``"values"``.
        dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
        plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
            ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
        cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
        title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
        show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
            directory.
        save_name: File name, including the extension. Default: ``"mesh.pdf"``.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty.
        TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

    """
    if mesh is None:
        mesh = self.meshes
        if mesh is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
            )

    idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

    if isinstance(mesh, list):
        mesh = mesh[idx]
    elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
        raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

    return plot_tatva_mesh(
        mesh,
        cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
        backend=backend,
        values=values,
        data_location=data_location,

    class MeshFEMBase(FEMBase, ABC):
    """A triangular surface mesh that can be replaced by a tetrahedral volume.

    ``CELL_TYPE`` is ``"triangle"`` until ``tetrahedralize`` runs, then
    ``"tetra"``. Tetrahedralization converts the stored coordinates from
    millimetres to metres.
    """

    # TODO: This shouldn't be capable of holding multiple meshes,
    #  but that seems counter to how the naming works. But, I'm not sure.
    def __init__(
        self,
        points: ArrayLike,
        elements: ArrayLike,
    ):
        """Store a surface or a tetrahedral volume.

        Three nodes per element make a triangular surface. Four nodes per element
        make a tetrahedral volume, and the exterior faces and outward normals are
        cached for later boundary queries.

        Args:
            points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``. Stored as ``float32``.
            elements: Connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)`` or ``(M, 4)``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)``, or if ``elements`` is
                neither ``(M, 3)`` nor ``(M, 4)``.

        """
        super().__init__()

        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        elements: np.ndarray = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)

        if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

        if elements.ndim != 2 or elements.shape[1] not in (3, 4):
            raise ValueError(
                "Expected triangular surface faces with shape (M, 3) or "
                f"tetrahedral elements with shape (M, 4), got {elements.shape}.",
            )

        self.boundary_faces: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.boundary_normals: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._surface_points: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._surface_faces: np.ndarray | None = None

        if elements.shape[1] == 3:
            self._set_surface_mesh(points, elements)
        else:
            self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

    @property
    def tetrahedralized(self) -> bool:
        """Report whether the stored mesh is a tetrahedral volume.

        Returns:
            ``True`` when ``CELL_TYPE`` is ``"tetra"``.

        """
        return self.CELL_TYPE == "tetra"

    def _set_surface_mesh(
        self,
        points: np.ndarray,
        faces: np.ndarray,
    ) -> None:
        self.CELL_TYPE = "triangle"
        self._surface_points = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self._surface_faces = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32).copy()
        self.boundary_faces = None
        self.boundary_normals = None
        self.meshes = Mesh(
            jnp.asarray(self._surface_points),
            elements=jnp.asarray(self._surface_faces),
        )

    def _set_tetrahedral_mesh(
        self,
        points: np.ndarray,
        elements: np.ndarray,
    ) -> None:
        self.CELL_TYPE = "tetra"
        points = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        elements = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)
        self.meshes = Mesh(
            jnp.asarray(points),
            elements=jnp.asarray(elements),
        )
        self.boundary_faces, self.boundary_normals = _boundary_geometry_from_arrays(
            points,
            elements,
            "tetra",
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _load_points_and_faces(
        file: str | Path,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        file = Path(file)
        file_type = file.suffix.lower().removeprefix(".")

        if file_type not in get_args(FileType):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid File Type. Got '{file_type}'.")

        match file_type:
            case "stl" | "ply":
                mesh = trimesh.load_mesh(file)

                points = np.asarray(
                    mesh.vertices,
                    dtype=np.float32,
                )
                faces = np.asarray(
                    mesh.faces,
                    dtype=np.int32,
                )

            case "h5" | "hdf5":
                with h5py.File(file, "r") as f:
                    points = np.asarray(
                        f["points"][:],
                        dtype=np.float32,
                    )
                    faces = np.asarray(
                        f["faces"][:],
                        dtype=np.int32,
                    )

            case "npz":
                with np.load(str(file)) as data:
                    points = np.asarray(
                        data["points"],
                        dtype=np.float32,
                    )
                    faces = np.asarray(
                        data["faces"],
                        dtype=np.int32,
                    )

        return points, faces

    @classmethod
    def from_file(
        cls,
        file: str | Path,
        *,
        tetrahedralize: bool = True,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Load a triangular surface from disk and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

        ``.stl`` and ``.ply`` are read with Trimesh. ``.h5``, ``.hdf5``, and
        ``.npz`` must contain ``points`` and ``faces`` arrays. ``kwargs`` are
        forwarded to ``from_points_and_faces``, including any extra arguments
        required by a subclass constructor.

        Args:
            file: Path of the surface mesh.
            tetrahedralize: Build a tetrahedral volume after loading.
                Default: ``True``.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to ``from_points_and_faces``, including any extra
                arguments required by a subclass constructor.

        Returns:
            A mesh of this class.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the suffix is not a supported file type, or if the
                loaded arrays are not a triangular surface.

        """
        points, faces = cls._load_points_and_faces(file)

        return cls.from_points_and_faces(
            points,
            faces,
            tetrahedralize=tetrahedralize,
            **kwargs,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_points_and_faces(
        cls,
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        tetrahedralize: bool = True,
        tetrahedralizer: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Build a mesh from a triangular surface and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

        ``kwargs`` are passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
        ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass can use
        them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

        Args:
            points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``.
            faces: Triangle connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)``.
            tetrahedralize: Replace the surface with a tetrahedral volume.
                Default: ``True``.
            tetrahedralizer: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
            target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
            quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
                Default: ``True``.
            **kwargs: Passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
                ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass
                can use them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

        Returns:
            A mesh of this class.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)`` or ``faces`` is not
                ``(M, 3)``.

        """
        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        faces: np.ndarray = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32)

        if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

        if faces.ndim != 2 or faces.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected triangular faces with shape (M, 3), got {faces.shape}.",
            )

        mesh = cls(
            points,
            faces,
            **kwargs,
        )

        if tetrahedralize:
            mesh.tetrahedralize(
                method=tetrahedralizer,
                target_size=target_size,
                quality=quality,
            )

        return mesh

    def tetrahedralize(
        self,
        *,
        method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        scale_factor: float | None = None,
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
        overwrite: bool = False,
    ):
        """Replace the stored triangular surface with a tetrahedral volume.

        The new node coordinates are the mesher output multiplied by ``1e-3``,
        converting millimetres to metres. A mesh that is already tetrahedral is
        left unchanged unless ``overwrite`` is set. The exterior faces and outward
        normals are cached.

        Args:
            method: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
            target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
            scale_factor: Scale the mesh by this factor. Default: ``None``.
            quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
                Default: ``True``.
            overwrite: Tetrahedralize again when a volume mesh is already stored.
                Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            This mesh.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no triangular surface is stored, or if ``method`` is
                unknown.

        """
        if self.tetrahedralized and not overwrite:
            return self

        if self._surface_points is None or self._surface_faces is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "No triangular surface mesh is available to tetrahedralize.",
            )

        points, elements = self._tetrahedralize(
            self._surface_points,
            self._surface_faces,
            method=method,
            target_size=target_size,
            quality=quality,
        )

        # the mesh is in mm, but the physics happens in m.
        points = points * scale_factor

        self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

        return self

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        match method:
            case "gmsh":
                return MeshFEMBase._tetrahedralize_gmsh(
                    points,
                    faces,
                    target_size=target_size,
                )

            case "tetgen":
                return MeshFEMBase._tetrahedralize_tetgen(
                    points,
                    faces,
                    quality=quality,
                )

            case _:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown tetrahedralization method: {method!r}.")

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize_tetgen(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        quality: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        points_array = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)
        faces_array = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32)
        tet = tetgen.TetGen(points_array, faces_array)
        tet.tetrahedralize(quality=quality)

        return (
            np.asarray(tet.node, dtype=np.float32),
            np.asarray(tet.elem, dtype=np.int32),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize_gmsh(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        target_size: float | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)
        faces: np.ndarray = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int64)

        if target_size is not None and target_size <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"target_size must be positive, got {target_size}.")

        was_initialized = bool(gmsh.isInitialized())

        if not was_initialized:
            gmsh.initialize()

        previous_model = gmsh.model.getCurrent() if was_initialized and gmsh.model.list() else None

        try:
            gmsh.model.add("mesh_fem_tetrahedralization")

            surface_tag = gmsh.model.addDiscreteEntity(2)

            node_tags = np.arange(
                1,
                points.shape[0] + 1,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            triangle_type = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementType(
                "Triangle",
                1,
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.addNodes(
                2,
                surface_tag,
                node_tags,
                points.reshape(-1),
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.addElementsByType(
                surface_tag,
                triangle_type,
                [],
                (faces + 1).reshape(-1),
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.reclassifyNodes()

            volume_tag = gmsh.model.addDiscreteEntity(
                3,
                boundary=[surface_tag],
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.createGeometry([(3, volume_tag)])

            gmsh.option.setNumber(
                "Mesh.MeshOnlyEmpty",
                1,
            )

            gmsh.option.setNumber(
                "Mesh.AngleToleranceFacetOverlap",
                0.01,
            )

            if target_size is not None:
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeFromPoints",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeFromCurvature",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeExtendFromBoundary",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeMin",
                    target_size,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeMax",
                    target_size,
                )

            gmsh.model.mesh.generate(3)

            node_tags, coords, _ = gmsh.model.mesh.getNodes()

            tetra_type = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementType(
                "Tetrahedron",
                1,
            )

            _, tetra_node_tags = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementsByType(
                tetra_type,
            )

            points_out = np.reshape(
                np.asarray(
                    coords,
                    dtype=np.float32,
                ),
                shape=(-1, 3),
            )

            node_tags: np.ndarray = np.asarray(
                node_tags,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            tetra_node_tags: np.ndarray = np.asarray(
                tetra_node_tags,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            node_indices: np.ndarray = np.empty(
                node_tags.max() + 1,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )
            node_indices[node_tags] = np.arange(node_tags.size)

            elements_out = node_indices[tetra_node_tags].reshape(-1, 4).astype(np.int32)

            return points_out, elements_out

        finally:
            if was_initialized:
                gmsh.model.remove()

                if previous_model is not None:
                    gmsh.model.setCurrent(previous_model)
            else:
                gmsh.finalize()

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_boundary_faces(
        points: ArrayLike,
        elements: ArrayLike,
    ) -> NDArray:
        boundary_faces, _ = _boundary_geometry_from_arrays(
            points,
            elements,
            "tetra",
        )
        return boundary_faces

    def boundary_geometry(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Return the exterior boundary of a mesh.

        The cached faces and normals are returned when ``mesh`` is the stored
        tetrahedral volume. Any other mesh is computed by ``FEMBase``.

        Args:
            mesh: Tatva mesh to query.

        Returns:
            Boundary connectivity and unit outward normals.

        """
        if (
            mesh is self.meshes
            and self.tetrahedralized
            and self.boundary_faces is not None
            and self.boundary_normals is not None
        ):
            return self.boundary_faces, self.boundary_normals

        return super().boundary_geometry(mesh)

    def __init__(
    self,
    points: ArrayLike,
    elements: ArrayLike,
):
    """Store a surface or a tetrahedral volume.

    Three nodes per element make a triangular surface. Four nodes per element
    make a tetrahedral volume, and the exterior faces and outward normals are
    cached for later boundary queries.

    Args:
        points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``. Stored as ``float32``.
        elements: Connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)`` or ``(M, 4)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)``, or if ``elements`` is
            neither ``(M, 3)`` nor ``(M, 4)``.

    """
    super().__init__()

    points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
    elements: np.ndarray = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)

    if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

    if elements.ndim != 2 or elements.shape[1] not in (3, 4):
        raise ValueError(
            "Expected triangular surface faces with shape (M, 3) or "
            f"tetrahedral elements with shape (M, 4), got {elements.shape}.",
        )

    self.boundary_faces: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.boundary_normals: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._surface_points: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._surface_faces: np.ndarray | None = None

    if elements.shape[1] == 3:
        self._set_surface_mesh(points, elements)
    else:
        self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

    def plot(
    self,
    *,
    backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
    ax=None,
    plotter=None,
    mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
    index: int | None = None,
    values=None,
    data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
    surface_elements=None,
    label: str = "values",
    dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
    plane: Plane = "xy",
    cmap: str = "managua",
    show_edges: bool = False,
    lighting: bool | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "mesh.pdf",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Plot one mesh, with no knowledge of where it came from.

    ``mesh=None`` uses ``self.meshes``. ``index`` selects an entry when that
    value is a list. ``values`` are colored on the nodes or the cells according
    to ``data_location``.

    Args:
        backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
        ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
        plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
        mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
        index: Entry to draw when ``mesh`` is a list. Default: the first entry.
        values: Scalar field to color. The mesh is drawn uncolored when omitted.
        data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. Required when ``values`` is
            set and the plotter cannot infer it.
        surface_elements: Optional face connectivity used instead of the mesh
            cells. Each row is one face.
        label: Color-bar label. Default: ``"values"``.
        dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
        plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
            ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
        cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
        title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
        show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
            directory.
        save_name: File name, including the extension. Default: ``"mesh.pdf"``.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty.
        TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

    """
    if mesh is None:
        mesh = self.meshes
        if mesh is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
            )

    idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

    if isinstance(mesh, list):
        mesh = mesh[idx]
    elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
        raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

    return plot_tatva_mesh(
        mesh,
        cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
        backend=backend,
        values=values,
        data_location=data_location,
        surface_elements=surface_elements,
        label=label,
        title=title,
        ax=ax,
        plotter=plotter,
        dimensionality=dimensionality,
        plane=plane,
        cmap=cmap,
        show_edges=show_edges,
        lighting=lighting,
        show=show,
        save=save,
        save_location=save_location,
        save_name=save_name,
        save_format=save_format,
        dpi=dpi,
    )

    def tetrahedralize(
    self,
    *,
    method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
    scale_factor: float | None = None,
    target_size: float | None = None,
    quality: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
):
    """Replace the stored triangular surface with a tetrahedral volume.

    The new node coordinates are the mesher output multiplied by ``1e-3``,
    converting millimetres to metres. A mesh that is already tetrahedral is
    left unchanged unless ``overwrite`` is set. The exterior faces and outward
    normals are cached.

    Args:
        method: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
        target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
        scale_factor: Scale the mesh by this factor. Default: ``None``.
        quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
            Default: ``True``.
        overwrite: Tetrahedralize again when a volume mesh is already stored.
            Default: ``False``.

    Returns:
        This mesh.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no triangular surface is stored, or if ``method`` is
            unknown.

    """
    if self.tetrahedralized and not overwrite:
        return self

    if self._surface_points is None or self._surface_faces is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "No triangular surface mesh is available to tetrahedralize.",
        )

    points, elements = self._tetrahedralize(
        self._surface_points,
        self._surface_faces,
        method=method,
        target_size=target_size,
        quality=quality,
    )

    # the mesh is in mm, but the physics happens in m.
    points = points * scale_factor

    self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

    return self

    class HeightMapFEMBase(FEMBase, ABC):
    """Base for FEM solvers whose meshes are generated from height maps.

    A missing thickness produces a triangular surface mesh.
    A supplied
    ``thickness`` extrudes the same height map into a layered hexahedral mesh.
    """

    height_channel: int = 0
    mask_channel: int | None = None
    channel_count: int | None = None

    grid_node_indices: np.ndarray | list[np.ndarray] | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        lx: float,
        ly: float,
        thickness: float | None = None,
        height_channel: int = 0,
        mask_channel: int | None = None,
        channel_count: int | None = None,
        height_scale: float = 1.0,
        thickness_steps: int = 4,
        surface_grading: float = 1.0,
    ):
        """Store the height-map domain. No mesh is built until ``generate_meshes``.

        ``thickness=None`` selects a triangular surface. A numeric ``thickness``
        selects a layered hexahedral solid and requires ``thickness_steps >= 2``
        and ``surface_grading >= 1``. ``surface_grading=1`` spaces the layers
        uniformly. Larger values pack layers toward the scanned surface.

        Args:
            lx: In-plane length of the height map along ``x``.
            ly: In-plane length of the height map along ``y``.
            thickness: Solid thickness below the scan. ``None`` builds a membrane.
                Default: ``None``.
            height_channel: Scan-image channel read as height. Default: ``0``.
            mask_channel: Optional scan channel used as a mask. Default: ``None``.
            channel_count: Number of channels in each scan image. Inferred when
                omitted.
            height_scale: Multiplier applied to the height channel. Default: ``1``.
            thickness_steps: Node layers through the solid, including both
                surfaces. Default: ``4``.
            surface_grading: Layer clustering toward the scanned surface.
                Default: ``1``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a solid mesh is requested with fewer than two thickness
                steps, or with ``surface_grading`` below ``1``.

        """
        super().__init__()

        self.lx = float(lx)
        self.ly = float(ly)
        self.thickness = None if thickness is None else float(thickness)
        self.CELL_TYPE: CellType = cast(
            "CellType",
            "triangle" if self.thickness is None else "hexahedron",
        )

        self.height_channel = int(height_channel)
        self.mask_channel = mask_channel
        self.channel_count = channel_count
        self.height_scale = float(height_scale)

        self.thickness_steps = int(thickness_steps)
        self.surface_grading = float(surface_grading)

        if self.thickness is not None:
            if self.thickness_steps < 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"thickness_steps must be at least 2, got {thickness_steps}.",
                )

            if self.surface_grading < 1.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    "surface_grading must be at least 1.0 (1.0 = uniform layers), "
                    f"got {surface_grading}.",
                )

        self.grid_node_indices = None
        self._scan_images = None

    @property
    def layer_profile(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the normalized height of each solid-mesh node layer.

        Values run from ``0`` at the substrate to ``1`` at the scanned surface.
        ``surface_grading=1`` spaces them uniformly. Larger values keep more layers
        near ``1``.

        Returns:
            Array of shape ``(thickness_steps,)``.

        """
        s = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, self.thickness_steps)

        if self.surface_grading == 1.0:
            return s

        return 1.0 - (1.0 - s) ** self.surface_grading

    def _height_batch(self, images: Array) -> Array:
        heights = height_maps_from_scan(
            images,
            self.height_channel,
            self.channel_count,
        )
        return jnp.asarray(heights) * self.height_scale

    def _generate_mesh(self, image: Array):
        image = jnp.asarray(image)
        if image.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected a (H, W) height map, got shape {tuple(image.shape)}.",
            )

        h, w = image.shape
        x = jnp.linspace(0.0, self.lx, w)
        y = jnp.linspace(0.0, self.ly, h)

        if self.thickness is None:
            yy, xx = jnp.meshgrid(y, x, indexing="ij")

            nodes = jnp.stack(
                [
                    xx,
                    yy,
                    image,
                ],
                axis=-1,
            ).reshape(-1, 3)

            grid_node_indices = np.arange(
                h * w,
                dtype=np.int32,
            ).reshape(h, w)

            elements = []
            for iy in range(h - 1):
                for ix in range(w - 1):
                    n00 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix]
                    n10 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1]
                    n01 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix]
                    n11 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1]

                    elements.append([n00, n10, n11])
                    elements.append([n00, n11, n01])

            elements = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32))
            return Mesh(nodes, elements=elements), grid_node_indices

        steps = self.thickness_steps
        eta = jnp.asarray(self.layer_profile)

        yy, xx, ee = jnp.meshgrid(
            y,
            x,
            eta,
            indexing="ij",
        )

        zz = ee * (self.thickness + image[..., None])

        nodes = jnp.stack(
            [
                xx,
                yy,
                zz,
            ],
            axis=-1,
        ).reshape(-1, 3)

        grid_node_indices = np.arange(
            h * w * steps,
            dtype=np.int32,
        ).reshape(h, w, steps)

        elements = []
        for iy in range(h - 1):
            for ix in range(w - 1):
                for iz in range(steps - 1):
                    n000 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix, iz]
                    n100 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1, iz]
                    n110 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1, iz]
                    n010 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix, iz]

                    n001 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix, iz + 1]
                    n101 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1, iz + 1]
                    n111 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1, iz + 1]
                    n011 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix, iz + 1]

                    elements.append(
                        [
                            n000,
                            n100,
                            n110,
                            n010,
                            n001,
                            n101,
                            n111,
                            n011,
                        ],
                    )

        elements = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32))
        return Mesh(nodes, elements=elements), grid_node_indices

    def generate_meshes(self, images: Array):
        """Build one Tatva mesh for each height map and store the pixel-to-node map.

        A single ``(H, W)`` map is stored as one mesh. A batch is stored as a list.
        Accepted layouts are ``(H, W)``, ``(N, H, W)``, ``(C, H, W)``, and
        ``(N, C, H, W)``. The height channel is multiplied by ``height_scale``.

        A membrane uses the height as ``z`` and splits each pixel quad into two
        triangles. A solid extrudes that surface through ``thickness`` into
        hexahedra. ``grid_node_indices`` records which node came from which pixel,
        with shape ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, thickness_steps)``.

        Args:
            images: One height map or a batch of scan images.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``images`` is not one of the accepted layouts, or if a
                single map is not two-dimensional after the height channel is read.

        """
        self._scan_images = scan_images_nchw(
            images,
            self.height_channel,
            self.channel_count,
        )
        images = jnp.asarray(self._height_batch(images))

        match images.ndim:
            case 2:
                self.meshes, self.grid_node_indices = self._generate_mesh(images)

            case 3:
                meshes, grid_node_indices = [], []

                for image in images:
                    mesh, grid_indices = self._generate_mesh(image)

                    meshes.append(mesh)
                    grid_node_indices.append(grid_indices)

                self.meshes = meshes
                self.grid_node_indices = grid_node_indices

            case _:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid image shape {tuple(images.shape)}. "
                    "Pass (H, W), (N, H, W), (C, H, W) or (N, C, H, W).",
                )

    def _plot_channel(self, channel: int | None) -> int:
        if channel is not None:
            return int(channel)
        return int(self.height_channel)

    def _node_values_for_plot(self, *, index: int, channel: int, n_nodes: int):
        return scan_channel_node_values(
            scan_images=self._scan_images,
            grid_node_indices=self.grid_node_indices,
            index=index,
            channel=channel,
            n_nodes=n_nodes,
        )

    def _channel_label(self, channel: int) -> str:
        if channel == self.height_channel:
            return "relative height [mm]"
        if channel == self.mask_channel:
            return "material mask"
        return f"channel {channel}"

    def _height_map_surface_elements(self, index: int = 0) -> np.ndarray | None:
        grid = (
            self.grid_node_indices[index]
            if isinstance(self.grid_node_indices, list)
            else self.grid_node_indices
        )

        if grid is None:
            return None

        grid: np.ndarray = np.asarray(grid)
        if grid.ndim == 2:
            return None

        if grid.ndim != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected grid_node_indices with 2 or 3 dimensions, got {grid.ndim}.",
            )

        surface = grid[..., -1]

        return np.reshape(
            np.stack(
                [
                    surface[:-1, :-1],
                    surface[:-1, 1:],
                    surface[1:, 1:],
                    surface[1:, :-1],
                ],
                axis=-1,
            ),
            (-1, 4),
        )

    def plot(
        self,
        *,
        backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        values=None,
        data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
        surface_elements=None,
        label: str = "values",
        channel: int | None = None,
        dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
        plane: Plane = "xy",
        cmap: str = "managua",
        show_edges: bool = False,
        lighting: bool | None = None,
        title: str | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "stress.pdf",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
    ):
        """Plot one height-map mesh, using the scan when no field is given.

        ``values=None`` samples ``channel`` onto the scanned surface. The default
        channel is the height channel. If no scan is stored, the node's ``z``
        coordinate is used instead. The drawn faces are the top surface of the
        mesh unless ``surface_elements`` is passed.

        Args:
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
            index: Crop to draw when several height maps were meshed.
                Default: the first crop.
            values: Scalar field to color. A scan channel is used when omitted.
            data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. A scan-derived field is
                plotted on the points.
            surface_elements: Faces to draw. Default: the scanned surface.
            label: Color-bar label. A scan channel replaces this with its own label.
            channel: Scan channel used when ``values`` is omitted. Default: the
                height channel.
            dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
            plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
                ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
            cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
            title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name, including the extension.
                Default: ``"stress.pdf"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty, or if
                ``channel`` is outside the stored scan.
            TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

        """
        if mesh is None:
            mesh = self.meshes
            if mesh is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
                )

        idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

        if isinstance(mesh, list):
            mesh = mesh[idx]
        elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

        if values is None:
            channel = self._plot_channel(channel)
            label = self._channel_label(channel)

            values = self._node_values_for_plot(
                index=idx,
                channel=channel,
                n_nodes=mesh.coords.shape[0],
            )

            if values is None:
                values = np.asarray(mesh.coords)[:, 2]

            data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] = "point"

        if surface_elements is None:
            surface_elements = self._height_map_surface_elements(idx)

        return super().plot(
            backend=backend,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            mesh=mesh,
            index=idx,
            values=values,
            data_location=data_location,
            surface_elements=surface_elements,
            label=label,
            dimensionality=dimensionality,
            plane=plane,
            cmap=cmap,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            lighting=lighting,
            title=title,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    lx: float,
    ly: float,
    thickness: float | None = None,
    height_channel: int = 0,
    mask_channel: int | None = None,
    channel_count: int | None = None,
    height_scale: float = 1.0,
    thickness_steps: int = 4,
    surface_grading: float = 1.0,
):
    """Store the height-map domain. No mesh is built until ``generate_meshes``.

    ``thickness=None`` selects a triangular surface. A numeric ``thickness``
    selects a layered hexahedral solid and requires ``thickness_steps >= 2``
    and ``surface_grading >= 1``. ``surface_grading=1`` spaces the layers
    uniformly. Larger values pack layers toward the scanned surface.

    Args:
        lx: In-plane length of the height map along ``x``.
        ly: In-plane length of the height map along ``y``.
        thickness: Solid thickness below the scan. ``None`` builds a membrane.
            Default: ``None``.
        height_channel: Scan-image channel read as height. Default: ``0``.
        mask_channel: Optional scan channel used as a mask. Default: ``None``.
        channel_count: Number of channels in each scan image. Inferred when
            omitted.
        height_scale: Multiplier applied to the height channel. Default: ``1``.
        thickness_steps: Node layers through the solid, including both
            surfaces. Default: ``4``.
        surface_grading: Layer clustering toward the scanned surface.
            Default: ``1``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a solid mesh is requested with fewer than two thickness
            steps, or with ``surface_grading`` below ``1``.

    """
    super().__init__()

    self.lx = float(lx)
    self.ly = float(ly)
    self.thickness = None if thickness is None else float(thickness)
    self.CELL_TYPE: CellType = cast(
        "CellType",
        "triangle" if self.thickness is None else "hexahedron",
    )

    self.height_channel = int(height_channel)
    self.mask_channel = mask_channel
    self.channel_count = channel_count
    self.height_scale = float(height_scale)

    self.thickness_steps = int(thickness_steps)
    self.surface_grading = float(surface_grading)

    if self.thickness is not None:
        if self.thickness_steps < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"thickness_steps must be at least 2, got {thickness_steps}.",
            )

        if self.surface_grading < 1.0:
            raise ValueError(
                "surface_grading must be at least 1.0 (1.0 = uniform layers), "
                f"got {surface_grading}.",
            )

    self.grid_node_indices = None
    self._scan_images = None

    def generate_meshes(self, images: Array):
    """Build one Tatva mesh for each height map and store the pixel-to-node map.

    A single ``(H, W)`` map is stored as one mesh. A batch is stored as a list.
    Accepted layouts are ``(H, W)``, ``(N, H, W)``, ``(C, H, W)``, and
    ``(N, C, H, W)``. The height channel is multiplied by ``height_scale``.

    A membrane uses the height as ``z`` and splits each pixel quad into two
    triangles. A solid extrudes that surface through ``thickness`` into
    hexahedra. ``grid_node_indices`` records which node came from which pixel,
    with shape ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, thickness_steps)``.

    Args:
        images: One height map or a batch of scan images.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``images`` is not one of the accepted layouts, or if a
            single map is not two-dimensional after the height channel is read.

    """
    self._scan_images = scan_images_nchw(
        images,
        self.height_channel,
        self.channel_count,
    )
    images = jnp.asarray(self._height_batch(images))

    match images.ndim:
        case 2:
            self.meshes, self.grid_node_indices = self._generate_mesh(images)

        case 3:
            meshes, grid_node_indices = [], []

            for image in images:
                mesh, grid_indices = self._generate_mesh(image)

                meshes.append(mesh)
                grid_node_indices.append(grid_indices)

            self.meshes = meshes
            self.grid_node_indices = grid_node_indices

        case _:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid image shape {tuple(images.shape)}. "
                "Pass (H, W), (N, H, W), (C, H, W) or (N, C, H, W).",
            )

    class ElasticityFEMMixin(FEMPhysics, ABC):
    """Linear-elasticity assembly and solve, independent of where the mesh came from.

    Subclasses supply the mesh. After ``solve``, ``displacement`` and ``stress``
    hold one array per mesh, or a single array when only one mesh is assigned.
    """

    CELL_TYPE: CellType
    ELEMENT: type
    N_DOFS_PER_NODE: int = 3
    meshes: Mesh | list[Mesh] | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        material: pinnjax.ElasticMaterial,
        conditions: MechanicalCondition | list[MechanicalCondition],
        *,
        solver: SolverBackend = "sparse",
        cg_rtol: float = CG_RTOL,
        cg_max_iter: int = CG_MAX_ITER,
        color_batch_size: int | None = 10,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Store the material, boundary conditions, and linear-solver settings.

        A single condition is wrapped in a list. ``kwargs`` are forwarded to the
        cooperating mesh base class.

        Args:
            material: Isotropic linear-elastic material. Uses ``youngs_modulus``
                and ``poissons_ratio``.
            conditions: Dirichlet and traction conditions applied during assembly.
            solver: Linear solver backend, ``"sparse"`` or ``"matrix_free"``.
                Default: ``"sparse"``.
            cg_rtol: Relative residual tolerance for conjugate gradient.
                Default: ``1e-8``.
            cg_max_iter: Maximum conjugate-gradient iterations.
                Default: ``20000``.
            color_batch_size: Element-color batch size passed to the linear solver.
                Default: ``10``.
            **kwargs: Forwarded extra arguments required by a subclass constructor.

        """
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

        self.material = material
        self.conditions = conditions if isinstance(conditions, list) else [conditions]
        self.solver = solver
        self.cg_rtol = float(cg_rtol)
        self.cg_max_iter = int(cg_max_iter)
        self.color_batch_size = color_batch_size

        self.stress: Array | list[Array] | None = None
        self.displacement: Array | list[Array] | None = None

    def _projector(self, operator: Operator):
        return None

    def _assemble_conditions(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
        operator: Operator,
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array, Array]:
        n_dofs: int = mesh.coords.shape[0] * self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE

        fixed_mask: np.ndarray = np.zeros(
            n_dofs,
            dtype=bool,
        )

        prescribed_displacement: Array = jnp.zeros(n_dofs)

        external_force: Array = jnp.zeros(n_dofs)

        for condition in self.conditions:
            contribution = condition.assemble(
                mesh,
                operator,
                cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
                n_dofs_per_node=self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE,
            )

            if contribution.fixed_dofs is not None:
                if contribution.fixed_values is None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{type(condition).__name__} returned fixed_dofs without fixed_values.",
                    )

                fixed_dofs: np.ndarray = np.asarray(
                    contribution.fixed_dofs,
                    dtype=np.int64,
                )

                fixed_values: Array = jnp.asarray(contribution.fixed_values)

                if fixed_values.shape != fixed_dofs.shape:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{type(condition).__name__} fixed_values must have "
                        f"shape {fixed_dofs.shape}. "
                        f"Got {fixed_values.shape}.",
                    )

                fixed_mask[fixed_dofs] = True

                prescribed_displacement = prescribed_displacement.at[fixed_dofs].set(
                    fixed_values,
                )

            elif contribution.fixed_values is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{type(condition).__name__} returned fixed_values without fixed_dofs.",
                )

            if contribution.external_force is not None:
                external_force = external_force + contribution.external_force

        fixed_dofs: Array = jnp.asarray(
            np.flatnonzero(fixed_mask),
            dtype=jnp.int32,
        )

        applied: Array = jnp.sum(jnp.abs(external_force))

        net: Array = jnp.sum(
            external_force.reshape(
                -1,
                self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE,
            ),
            axis=0,
        )

        config.LOGGER.info(
            f"  Net applied force: {np.asarray(net)} N "
            f"({float(jnp.linalg.norm(net) / jnp.maximum(applied, 1e-30)):.2e} "
            "of the applied load)",
        )

        return (
            fixed_dofs,
            prescribed_displacement,
            external_force,
        )

    def _solve_mesh(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
    ):
        element = self.ELEMENT()
        operator = Operator(mesh, element)
        projector = self._projector(operator)

        def elasticity_response(_displacement: Array):
            if projector is None:
                return isotropic_linear_elasticity(
                    operator=operator,
                    displacement=_displacement,
                    material=self.material,
                )

            return isotropic_linear_elasticity(
                operator=operator,
                displacement=_displacement,
                material=self.material,
                projector=projector,
            )

        @jax.jit
        def total_energy_full(u_flat: Array) -> Array:
            _displacement = u_flat.reshape(
                -1,
                self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE,
            )

            _stress, _strain = elasticity_response(_displacement)

            energy_density = 0.5 * jnp.einsum(
                "...ij,...ij->...",
                _stress,
                _strain,
            )

            return operator.integrate(energy_density)

        n_dofs: int = mesh.coords.shape[0] * self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE

        (
            fixed_dofs,
            prescribed_displacement,
            f_ext_full,
        ) = self._assemble_conditions(mesh, operator)

        fixed_dofs_np: np.ndarray = np.asarray(fixed_dofs, dtype=np.int64)

        free_mask: np.ndarray = np.ones(n_dofs, dtype=bool)
        free_mask[fixed_dofs_np] = False

        free_dofs: Array = jnp.asarray(np.flatnonzero(free_mask), dtype=jnp.int32)

        @jax.jit
        def total_energy(
            u_free: Array,
        ) -> Array:
            _u_full: Array = prescribed_displacement.at[free_dofs].set(u_free)
            return total_energy_full(_u_full)

        internal_force = jax.jacrev(total_energy)

        f_ext: Array = f_ext_full[free_dofs]

        u_sol, norm_res = solve_linear(
            self.solver,
            u=jnp.zeros_like(f_ext),
            fext=f_ext,
            gradient=internal_force,
            mesh=mesh,
            n_dofs_per_node=self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE,
            free_dofs=free_dofs,
            color_batch_size=self.color_batch_size,
            cg_rtol=self.cg_rtol,
            cg_max_iter=self.cg_max_iter,
        )

        u_full: Array = prescribed_displacement.at[free_dofs].set(u_sol)

        displacement: Array = u_full.reshape(-1, self.N_DOFS_PER_NODE)

        stress, _ = elasticity_response(displacement)

        return displacement, norm_res, stress

    def solve(self):
        """Solve linear-elastic equilibrium on each assigned mesh.

        Stores the nodal displacement and the stress tensor on ``displacement`` and
        ``stress``. One mesh produces one displacement array of shape ``(N, 3)`` and
        a scalar residual norm. A list of meshes produces a list of displacement
        arrays and a stacked vector of residual norms.

        Returns:
            Displacement and the linear-solver residual norm. Both are lists when
            ``meshes`` is a list; the residual norms are then stacked into one array.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If no mesh has been assigned or generated.
            TypeError: If ``meshes`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

        """
        if self.meshes is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "A mesh must be assigned or generated before it can be solved.",
            )

        if isinstance(self.meshes, Mesh):
            displacement, norm_res, stress = self._solve_mesh(self.meshes)

            self.displacement = displacement
            self.stress = stress

            return displacement, norm_res

        if isinstance(self.meshes, list):
            displacements = []
            stresses = []
            residuals = []

            for mesh in self.meshes:
                displacement, norm_res, stress = self._solve_mesh(mesh)

                displacements.append(displacement)
                stresses.append(stress)
                residuals.append(norm_res)

            self.displacement = displacements
            self.stress = stresses

            return displacements, jnp.stack(residuals)

        raise TypeError(f"Unexpected meshes type: {type(self.meshes).__name__}")

    def plot_stress(
        self,
        component: Literal[
            "xx",
            "yy",
            "zz",
            "xy",
            "xz",
            "yz",
            "von_mises",
        ] = "von_mises",
        *,
        backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        index: int | None = None,
        dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
        plane: Plane = "xy",
        cmap: str = "managua",
        stress_scale: float = 1.0,
        norm=None,
        boundaries=None,
        averaging: Literal["element", "nodal"] = "element",
        show_edges: bool = False,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "stress",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
        title: str | bool | None = True,
    ):
        """Plot one stress component on the solved mesh.

        ``index`` selects an entry when ``meshes`` is a list. ``None`` selects the
        first mesh. ``averaging="element"`` colors cells by the element stress.
        ``averaging="nodal"`` averages that stress onto the nodes first.
        ``stress_scale`` divides the plotted values.

        ``title=True`` uses the component label. ``title=False`` or ``None`` hides
        the title. A string sets a custom title.

        Args:
            component: Stress component to reduce to a scalar. One of ``"xx"``,
                ``"yy"``, ``"zz"``, ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, ``"yz"``, or
                ``"von_mises"``. Default: ``"von_mises"``.
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            index: Mesh and stress entry to plot when several meshes are stored.
                Default: the first entry.
            dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
            plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
                ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
            cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
            stress_scale: Divisor applied to the plotted stress. Default: ``1``.
            norm: Matplotlib or PyVista normalization. Built from ``boundaries``
                when omitted.
            boundaries: Contour levels used to build a boundary norm.
            averaging: ``"element"`` or ``"nodal"``. Default: ``"element"``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name without the extension. Default: ``"stress"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.
            title: ``True``, ``False``, ``None``, or a custom title string.
                Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If the mesh is missing, or ``solve`` has not been called.

        """
        if self.meshes is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Mesh must be assigned or generated before plotting.")

        if self.stress is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Solver must be solved before plotting stress.")

        idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

        if isinstance(self.meshes, list):
            mesh = self.meshes[idx]
            stress = self.stress[idx]

        elif isinstance(self.meshes, Mesh):
            mesh = self.meshes
            stress = self.stress

        else:
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected meshes type: {type(self.meshes).__name__}")

        return plot_fem_stress(
            mesh,
            stress,
            cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
            component=component,
            averaging=averaging,
            stress_scale=stress_scale,
            backend=backend,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            dimensionality=dimensionality,
            plane=plane,
            cmap=cmap,
            norm=norm,
            boundaries=boundaries,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
            title=title,
        )

        boundaries: Contour levels used to build a boundary norm.
        averaging: ``"element"`` or ``"nodal"``. Default: ``"element"``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
            directory.
        save_name: File name without the extension. Default: ``"stress"``.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.
        title: ``True``, ``False``, ``None``, or a custom title string.
            Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the mesh is missing, or ``solve`` has not been called.

    """
    if self.meshes is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Mesh must be assigned or generated before plotting.")

    if self.stress is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Solver must be solved before plotting stress.")

    idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

    if isinstance(self.meshes, list):
        mesh = self.meshes[idx]
        stress = self.stress[idx]

    elif isinstance(self.meshes, Mesh):
        mesh = self.meshes
        stress = self.stress

    else:
        raise TypeError(f"Unexpected meshes type: {type(self.meshes).__name__}")

    return plot_fem_stress(
        mesh,
        stress,
        cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
        component=component,
        averaging=averaging,
        stress_scale=stress_scale,
        backend=backend,
        ax=ax,
        plotter=plotter,
        dimensionality=dimensionality,
        plane=plane,
        cmap=cmap,
        norm=norm,
        boundaries=boundaries,
        show_edges=show_edges,
        show=show,
        save=save,
        save_location=save_location,
        save_name=save_name,
        save_format=save_format,
        dpi=dpi,
        title=title,
    )

    def solve(self):
    """Solve linear-elastic equilibrium on each assigned mesh.

    Stores the nodal displacement and the stress tensor on ``displacement`` and
    ``stress``. One mesh produces one displacement array of shape ``(N, 3)`` and
    a scalar residual norm. A list of meshes produces a list of displacement
    arrays and a stacked vector of residual norms.

    Returns:
        Displacement and the linear-solver residual norm. Both are lists when
        ``meshes`` is a list; the residual norms are then stacked into one array.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If no mesh has been assigned or generated.
        TypeError: If ``meshes`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

    """
    if self.meshes is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "A mesh must be assigned or generated before it can be solved.",
        )

    if isinstance(self.meshes, Mesh):
        displacement, norm_res, stress = self._solve_mesh(self.meshes)

        self.displacement = displacement
        self.stress = stress

        return displacement, norm_res

    if isinstance(self.meshes, list):
        displacements = []
        stresses = []
        residuals = []

        for mesh in self.meshes:
            displacement, norm_res, stress = self._solve_mesh(mesh)

            displacements.append(displacement)
            stresses.append(stress)
            residuals.append(norm_res)

        self.displacement = displacements
        self.stress = stresses

        return displacements, jnp.stack(residuals)

    raise TypeError(f"Unexpected meshes type: {type(self.meshes).__name__}")

    class ElasticityMeshFEMSolver(ElasticityFEMMixin, MeshFEMBase):
    """Linear elasticity on one existing tetrahedral mesh.

    ``elements`` must have shape ``(M, 4)``. A surface mesh has to be
    tetrahedralized before it can be passed to ``from_mesh``.
    """

    CELL_TYPE: CellType = "tetra"
    ELEMENT = Tetrahedron4

    def __init__(
        self,
        points: ArrayLike,
        elements: ArrayLike,
        material: pinnjax.ElasticMaterial,
        conditions: MechanicalCondition | list[MechanicalCondition],
        *,
        solver: SolverBackend = "sparse",
        cg_rtol: float = CG_RTOL,
        cg_max_iter: int = CG_MAX_ITER,
        color_batch_size: int | None = 10,
    ):
        """Build a tetrahedral elasticity solver from points and elements.

        Args:
            points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``.
            elements: Tetrahedron connectivity, shape ``(M, 4)``.
            material: Isotropic linear-elastic material.
            conditions: Dirichlet and traction conditions applied during assembly.
            solver: Linear solver backend, ``"sparse"`` or ``"matrix_free"``.
                Default: ``"sparse"``.
            cg_rtol: Relative residual tolerance for conjugate gradient.
                Default: ``1e-8``.
            cg_max_iter: Maximum conjugate-gradient iterations.
                Default: ``20000``.
            color_batch_size: Element-color batch size passed to the linear solver.
                Default: ``10``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``elements`` is not a tetrahedral connectivity array
                of shape ``(M, 4)``.

        """
        elements_array: np.ndarray = np.asarray(elements)
        if elements_array.ndim != 2 or elements_array.shape[1] != 4:
            raise ValueError(
                "ElasticityMeshFEMSolver requires a tetrahedralized mesh with "
                f"elements shaped (M, 4), got {elements_array.shape}.",
            )

        super().__init__(
            material=material,
            conditions=conditions,
            solver=solver,
            cg_rtol=cg_rtol,
            cg_max_iter=cg_max_iter,
            color_batch_size=color_batch_size,
            points=points,
            elements=elements,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_mesh(
        cls,
        mesh: MeshFEMBase,
        *,
        material: pinnjax.ElasticMaterial,
        conditions: MechanicalCondition | list[MechanicalCondition],
        solver: SolverBackend = "sparse",
        cg_rtol: float = CG_RTOL,
        cg_max_iter: int = CG_MAX_ITER,
        color_batch_size: int | None = 10,
    ):
        """Build a solver from a tetrahedralized ``MeshFEMBase``.

        The source must contain exactly one Tatva mesh, and
        ``mesh.tetrahedralize()`` must already have been called.

        Args:
            mesh: Tetrahedral volume mesh to copy points and elements from.
            material: Isotropic linear-elastic material.
            conditions: Dirichlet and traction conditions applied during assembly.
            solver: Linear solver backend, ``"sparse"`` or ``"matrix_free"``.
                Default: ``"sparse"``.
            cg_rtol: Relative residual tolerance for conjugate gradient.
                Default: ``1e-8``.
            cg_max_iter: Maximum conjugate-gradient iterations.
                Default: ``20000``.
            color_batch_size: Element-color batch size passed to the linear solver.
                Default: ``10``.

        Returns:
            An ``ElasticityMeshFEMSolver`` for that mesh.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If ``mesh`` is not a ``MeshFEMBase``, or if it does not
                hold exactly one Tatva mesh.
            ValueError: If the mesh has not been tetrahedralized.

        """
        if not isinstance(mesh, MeshFEMBase):
            raise TypeError(f"Expected MeshFEMBase, got {type(mesh).__name__}.")

        if not mesh.tetrahedralized:
            raise ValueError(
                "The mesh must be tetrahedralized before constructing an "
                "ElasticityMeshFEMSolver. Run 'mesh.tetrahedralize()' first.",
            )

        if not isinstance(mesh.meshes, Mesh):
            raise TypeError("Expected MeshFEMBase to contain exactly one Tatva mesh.")

        return cls(
            points=np.asarray(mesh.meshes.coords),
            elements=np.asarray(mesh.meshes.elements),
            material=material,
            conditions=conditions,
            solver=solver,
            cg_rtol=cg_rtol,
            cg_max_iter=cg_max_iter,
            color_batch_size=color_batch_size,
        )

    def write_mesh_to_abaqus(
        self,
        index: int = 0,
        save_location: Path | str | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = None,
    ):
        """Write one tetrahedral mesh as an Abaqus input file.

        The file is a single part. Nodes are 1-based, and the element keyword
        written by this method is ``C3D8``. ``save_location=None`` uses the
        working directory. ``save_name=None`` uses ``mesh-{index}.inp``. The name
        is used as given; the suffix is not added for you.

        Args:
            index: Mesh to export when ``meshes`` is a list. Default: ``0``.
            save_location: Output directory. Created if it does not exist.
            save_name: File name, including the extension.
                Default: ``mesh-{index}.inp``.

        Returns:
            Path of the written ``.inp`` file.

        Raises:
            AttributeError: If no mesh has been assigned.

        """
        if self.meshes is None:
            raise AttributeError(
                "No meshes associated with this solver.\n"
                "Make sure to run 'solver.generate_meshes()'.",
            )

        mesh = self.meshes[index] if isinstance(self.meshes, list) else self.meshes

        coords: np.ndarray = np.asarray(mesh.coords)
        elements: np.ndarray = np.asarray(mesh.elements)

        out_dir = Path(save_location) if save_location else Path.cwd()
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        filename = out_dir / (save_name or f"mesh-{index}.inp")

        with open(filename, "w") as f:
            f.write("*Heading\n")
            f.write("** Generated from tatva.Mesh\n")
            f.write("*Part, name=PART-1\n")

            f.write("*Node\n")
            f.writelines(
                f"{i}, {xyz[0]}, {xyz[1]}, {xyz[2]}\n" for i, xyz in enumerate(coords, start=1)
            )

            f.write("*Element, type=C3D8\n")
            for i, element in enumerate(elements, start=1):
                nodes = ", ".join(str(int(n) + 1) for n in element)
                f.write(f"{i}, {nodes}\n")

            f.write("*End Part\n")

        return filename

    def boundary_geometry(
    self,
    mesh: Mesh,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return the exterior boundary of a mesh.

    The cached faces and normals are returned when ``mesh`` is the stored
    tetrahedral volume. Any other mesh is computed by ``FEMBase``.

    Args:
        mesh: Tatva mesh to query.

    Returns:
        Boundary connectivity and unit outward normals.

    """
    if (
        mesh is self.meshes
        and self.tetrahedralized
        and self.boundary_faces is not None
        and self.boundary_normals is not None
    ):
        return self.boundary_faces, self.boundary_normals

    return super().boundary_geometry(mesh)

            arguments required by a subclass constructor.

            loaded arrays are not a triangular surface.

    points, faces = cls._load_points_and_faces(file)

        points,
        faces,
        tetrahedralize=tetrahedralize,
        **kwargs,
    )
